# Client-Scheduler PR conventions

Grounded in the repo's two merged PRs to date (both authored via Claude Code): #2 `feat(invitations):
add invitation-only booking service` and #3 `fix(ci): repair android-build.yml workflow and Flutter
v2 embedding`. (PR #1, from a different tool/author, was closed unmerged and doesn't reflect this
repo's house style — don't model titles on it.)

## Title format

Conventional-commit style, lowercase type + parenthesized scope + colon + imperative summary:
- `feat(invitations): add invitation-only booking service`
- `fix(ci): repair android-build.yml workflow and Flutter v2 embedding`
Pick the scope from the touched area (`invitations`, `ci`, `booking`, `analytics`, etc.), not the
file name.

## Description sections actually used

Neither merged PR uses a fixed template; sections are chosen per-PR:
- #2: a two-sentence prose intro (what the feature does, end to end) followed by a flat bullet list
  of what was added, one bullet per file/concern (model, repository, each new screen, router
  change) — no headers at all.
- #3: `## Summary` (numbered list, one root cause per fix, each with the exact error message
  encountered), then `## Testing` (a short before/after log of what was re-run and its result).
- Only add `## Summary`/`## Testing` headers for a fix-oriented PR like #3; a feature PR reads fine
  as #2's heading-free bullet list.

## Detail level

Model on #3: every claimed fix names the exact file changed and quotes the exact error string that
proved the bug and the fix (e.g. `Unrecognized named-value: 'secrets'`) — don't assert something
was fixed without the evidence that shows it.

## Tone & audience

Terse and technical, written for a reviewer who will read the diff — no marketing language, no
emoji, present-tense/imperative bullets ("Adds", "Fixes", not "This PR adds").

## Checklist

- End with the session link line these two PRs both use: `https://claude.ai/code/session_...`
  (#3 phrases it as `_Generated by [Claude Code](...)_`).
- State which files were touched when it clarifies scope; state what testing was attempted (and if
  a tool wasn't available, say so plainly, as #1 did — don't imply verification that didn't happen.
